text: Make Dilli Darshan: an open-world driving game set in Delhi, built from real map data, with rich Delhi assets. It must feel polished and rich. The old Barcelona game at ~/Desktop/code/delhi-drive felt thin and broken at base level: roads, terrain, overlaps, railings, the mirror axis. Do not trust its code.

Phase 0, part 1: do a SALVAGE AUDIT of the old repo, read only. Tell me what is worth keeping (data sources, bake knowledge, car tuning, tests, good assets, the lessons in its docs and TODO) and what is broken and why.
Phase 0, part 2: STYLE DISCOVERY with me. Compare style options side by side on look, feel and measured performance, with test scenes. Loop with me until I sign off.

Phase 0, part 3: ARCHITECTURE DISCOVERY. Compare engine and system options with measurements on this machine, for me to sign off. Cover WebGL vs WebGPU renderer, physics in a worker, the road graph to junction mesh builder, terrain that conforms to roads, tile streaming, instancing, LOD, KTX2 textures and perf budgets. I want the best and most optimized system for the browser.
After I sign off, I do nothing manual. You handle everything. Art, texture and sound needs go on the dashboard as cards with prompts.
Remove the old mirror idea entirely. Correct coordinates from day 1, with tests that a landmark lands in the right place, collisions match visuals, and north is up.

Source map data is broken, OSM and the rest. I accept that. Build an intermediate MAP REPAIR LAYER that finds what is broken and fixes it: roads, intersections, footpaths, buildings, rail and metro, foot over bridges, flyovers. For example links that should join, roads not touching the ground, flyovers that end in mid air. Start on a pilot area: Connaught Place, the ITO and Pragati Maidan flyovers, Chandni Chowk and one metro line, then scale up. I sign it off with the architecture.

Roads need a real lane-level model. OSM centrelines meet at one shared node, so in the old game merging and splitting carriageways collapsed into each other. Make roads lane sets with widths from lanes, width or Delhi road class defaults. Diverges and merges get proper tapers and gore areas, lanes shift sideways and never share an index point. On a flyover the centre lanes climb while the left and right service lanes stay at grade, and side lanes taper into the next flyover start. Build junctions from lane-edge curves with corner radii and no overlapping faces. Check for overlapping road faces, lane continuity through every split and merge, and taper length per road class. This is the top Fable task.

I want a MAP INSPECTOR: a separate 3D page linked from the dashboard. Show the repaired map with every issue marked. When I click an issue the camera flies there and I see your proposed fixes as 3D preview lines (connect to road A, connect to road B, terminate here, remove), each with a confidence score and your reasoning. I pick one or type a note, and it goes into the per-tile overrides that survive re-bakes, and into the inbox. Handle clear cases yourself and only queue the unclear or high-impact ones, sorted by impact. Also show lane widths, splits and merges so I can check ramps. Build it early, right after the architecture sign-off, so I can review during the pilot.

Let's change the style of it a little bit. Like the font and all for this localhost one. It looks like the other one that I made. Let's use the font S-A-A-N-S. It's in my downloads. Use that font. Use the black color or like a dark color, not this bluish tint and all. Make it cool looking. cool subtle minimal getting the job done. Impressive.

Direction change. Add a third discovery to Phase 0: GAME DESIGN DISCOVERY, with the same rules as style and architecture (interview me, compare options side by side, loop until I sign off, record the sign-off). Phase 0 cannot close without it. The problem: a car that drives around Delhi is a tech demo, not a game. Free roam alone gives no reason to play for an hour or come back tomorrow. I want Dilli Darshan to have a real core loop, built from what makes Delhi Delhi. Work through these with me: 1. The fantasy (new auto driver, delivery rider, cabbie who knows every gali, tourist guide, street racer, a mix; one sentence each plus why it fits Delhi). 2. The core loop at 30 seconds, 5 minutes, 1 hour; where tension comes from (traffic, time, money, rivals, police, weather, fares). 3. Missions and activities: a big list of Delhi-flavoured ideas (fares, deliveries, races, chases, festivals, wedding baraat routes, monsoon floods, rush hour, night runs, sightseeing tours past real landmarks, side jobs, collectibles), ranked by fun, uniqueness, effort to build and map reuse. 4. Progression and reasons to return (money, vehicle unlocks and upgrades, reputation by area, unlocking parts of the city, daily and weekly jobs, story or characters, personal bests and leaderboards, photo spots); which are healthy and which feel like chores. 5. Game feel (speed sense, near misses, horn culture, weaving through traffic, drifts, landmarks as rewards); name 3 feel pillars every feature must serve. 6. Scope honestly: smallest first playable loop that is already fun in the pilot area, then what grows from it; for each option fun, cost, risk, and needs from map, AI traffic and art. 7. References: compare known open world and driving games, what fits and what to avoid; inspiration, never copy. Output: harness/design/GAME_DESIGN_OPTIONS.md with comparison tables; after my sign-off GAME.md updated with fantasy, core loop, pillars, mission list and progression plan, plus a decisions.md entry; from then on the planner checks every phase against the pillars, and every mission gets acceptance criteria for fun as well as function (clear goal, fair fail, a reason to retry, a reward that matters). Ask me the questions in rounds, short and clear. Show examples and sketches where it helps. Do not build any mission system until I sign off.

Direction change: Delhi must look like Delhi, area by area. Add two data layers on top of the repaired map, and include both in Phase 0 architecture and style discovery so I can sign off on the approach. 1. LANDMARK REGISTRY: a list of every notable monument and famous building in Delhi with exact location and footprint (ASI protected monuments, Wikidata and Wikipedia entries, OSM historic, tourism and religious tags, plus well known modern ones: India Gate, Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Humayun's Tomb, Lotus Temple, Akshardham, Jama Masjid, Rashtrapati Bhavan, Connaught Place, Lodhi Garden tombs, Hauz Khas, metro stations, major markets, stadiums, malls). Stored as data (harness/data/landmarks.json or similar): name, lat/lon, footprint, height, era, importance tier, references (photos and descriptions to study), licence notes. Tiers: hero (hand built detailed model, recognisable from the road at driving speed), signature (simpler model, right silhouette and colour), marker (correct footprint and massing with the right material). Each landmark sits exactly where it really is, oriented correctly, with its real surroundings (gardens, walls, gates, parking, crowds). Landmark models and textures go on the dashboard as art cards with prompts and reference notes; procedural stand-ins until then. Hero landmarks double as navigation and as mission and photo spots. 2. AREA PROFILES (district character): divide Delhi into areas (wards, colonies, or zones from open data such as Master Plan land use, census and ward data, OSM land use, building footprint density, satellite greenery NDVI and night lights). Each area gets a profile: building types and their mix (Lutyens bungalows, kothis, builder floors, DDA flats, gated societies, urban villages, unauthorised colonies, old city havelis, commercial complexes, markets, malls, industrial); typical heights, colours, materials, balconies, water tanks, wires and signage density; greenery and tree types; road condition and cleanliness; street life (vendors, rickshaws, parked cars, pedestrians, stray animals); traffic mix and density by time of day; noise and ambience; wealth level as visual detail. A procedural generator builds ordinary buildings and street dressing from the profile, so Old Delhi feels like Old Delhi, Lutyens like Lutyens, Gurgaon-side societies like societies, and markets like markets, with smooth edges between areas. Profiles are data files Claude can tune and I can review on the map inspector (colour the map by area, click an area to see and edit its profile). Portray every community with respect and accuracy, based on data and reference, never caricature. Variety and life, not stereotypes. 3. HOW IT FITS: pilot first (profile and build the pilot area: Connaught Place, ITO, Chandni Chowk, one metro line, plus 2 or 3 hero landmarks), measure performance, then scale. Performance: instancing, LOD and texture atlases per area kit, within the signed off budgets. Fable tier: the area profile generator and the landmark placement pipeline. Verification: each landmark in the right place against real coordinates; side-by-side shots of each pilot area against reference photos, read by eye; area profiles visibly different from each other. Write the plan into harness/design/DELHI_WORLD.md, add the needed tasks after the map repair pilot, and ask me in rounds about which landmarks matter most to me and which areas to do first.
